post.summary: Exchange an API key for a short-lived Vijil JWT
post.description: Headless OAuth-2 client-credentials-style exchange. The CLI / SDK / CI presents `(client_id, client_secret)` minted via `POST /v1/api-keys` and receives a Vijil-signed JWT whose shape is identical to the JWTs issued by `/v1/auth/jwt/login` and the OAuth callback. Downstream middleware accepts all three interchangeably. Unauthenticated (no Authorization header required) — the key pair is the credential.

post.summary: Exchange a PKCE auth_code for a short-lived Vijil JWT
post.description: PKCE handoff completion. The CLI presents an `auth_code` it caught at its localhost callback (after the user finished console sign-in and consent) and the `code_verifier` it generated at the start of the flow. On success the endpoint returns a Vijil-signed JWT whose shape is byte-identical to the JWT issued by `/v1/auth/jwt/login` and `/v1/auth/token` — downstream middleware accepts all three interchangeably. Unauthenticated (no Authorization header required) — the auth_code + verifier ARE the credentials. Generic 401 on every failure mode (unknown code, wrong verifier, expired, deleted user) so an attacker can't enumerate which failed.

post.summary: Grant a SPIFFE enrollment token to a cohort of agents
post.description:
Bind each agent's SPIFFE identity and mint its enrollment token, as one operator action.

Requires agent:write in ``team_id``, checked once for the whole cohort. Per agent the bind
and the mint are one atomic unit, so a failure never leaves an agent half-granted. Duplicate
ids collapse to their first occurrence.

An unconfigured registrar fails the whole request with 503 before any agent is touched:
every mint would fail on it anyway, and reporting it as N per-agent errors would hide a
deployment-wide outage behind a 200.

The request is bounded by ``bulk_enrollment_deadline_seconds`` both in total and per agent,
because a token minted after the caller's connection is gone is a live credential nobody
holds. Agents that never got their turn are reported ``deadline_exceeded`` and the response
carries ``Retry-After``.

200.description: Per-agent outcomes. Returned even when NO agent was granted, so a client must inspect `granted_count` rather than branching on the status code alone. One agent's failure never blocks its siblings. Key results by `agent_id`, not by position: duplicate ids collapse, so `results` has `distinct_count` entries, which is below `requested_count` when the request repeated an id. To retry, resend only the ids whose `status` was not `granted` — a retried agent is minted a fresh token and its previous outstanding one is superseded. Every `token` is shown exactly once; the response is `Cache-Control: no-store` and must not be logged.

put.description:
Register where the agent runs and which image it is. Requires agent:write in ``team_id``.

The body is the runtime descriptor; ``runtime.account_id`` must be an AWS account connected to
the team and verified (``POST /v1/aws-accounts/{account_id}/verify``); 400 otherwise. The agent
must be deployed BY DIGEST: ``image_repository`` carries no tag or digest,
``image_digest`` is ``sha256:<64 lowercase hex>``, and the workload must run
``<image_repository>@<image_digest>`` (for AgentCore, the runtime's container URI) or SPIRE /
the delegate will not match it.

The account is verified again first (Console assumes its attestor role), so an account whose
trust policy no longer admits this team is demoted and refused (400).

The SPIRE registrar is called first and the runtime is recorded only once it confirms
(register-before-persist, fail-closed): 503/502 means nothing was recorded. The same write
binds the agent's canonical SVID ``spiffe://<td>/org/<team_id>/agent/<agent_id>``; for AgentCore
the execution role (as STS reports it, ``arn:aws:iam::<account>:role/<name>``) becomes the
agent's attested principal and must not belong to another agent (409). Idempotent: PUT the
same descriptor again to re-register.

The response carries the agent version (VIJIL-1595): ``version`` is Vijil's counter for the
agent, one per distinct (image digest, composition hash) pair, reused when the same pair is
registered again. ``process_reference_digest`` is
SHA-256 hex over the versioned encoding of ``image_digest`` (measured by SPIRE / AWS) and the
agent's current composition hash ``composition_sha256`` (declared: Console's record), with
``process_reference_version`` naming the encoding. Re-registering after the image or the
composition changed binds a new version and digest. 400 when the agent's composition cannot be
hashed; 409 when a concurrent registration of the same agent created the same version.

get.description:
Return ``{"runtime": <descriptor>}`` or ``{"runtime": null}``.

The descriptor is exactly the ``runtime`` object sent to the registrar: ``kind``,
``account_id``, ``region``, ``image_repository``, ``image_digest`` and the one block ``kind``
names. Other fields may be added beside ``runtime`` at the top level; ignore unknown keys.

Beside ``runtime`` (VIJIL-1595): ``version`` (the agent version the runtime is bound to),
``process_reference_digest`` and ``process_reference_version``
(null for a runtime registered before digests existed, and when ``runtime`` is null),
``composition_sha256`` (the composition hash registration bound) and ``composition_current``
(false once the agent's composition changed since, or when no digest was bound). The digest's
image half is measured by SPIRE / AWS; its composition half is Console's declaration. A stale
digest is reported, never enforced.

**Identity delegate** (``X-Webhook-Api-Key``, its service key, as for resolve-principal;
``team_id`` optional and, when given, must be the agent's team):

- 200 ``{"runtime": {...}}``: a registered runtime in a connected, verified account.
- 200 ``{"runtime": null}``: ONLY for an existing, visible agent with no registered runtime.
- 404: the agent does not exist, is archived or a Discover record never activated, or
  ``team_id`` is not its team.
- 409 ``{"detail", "code": "runtime_account_unverified", "reason": "not_connected" |
  "unverified", "account_id"}``: the agent has a runtime but its account is not a connected,
  verified account of its team. Never reported as ``runtime: null``; fail closed.

**Operators** (JWT with agent:read in ``team_id``, required): the same envelope, with the
runtime they registered whatever its account's state (so they can see what to verify);
``{"runtime": null}`` when there is none; 404 when the agent is not in the team.

get.description:
Returns what Console knows about the agent bound to the given SVID: the agent, its tenant, its attestation status, and the score, date and identity provenance of its latest completed evaluation. Facts only — no threshold and no verdict.

**Authorization** is scoped to the resolved agent's team. Global grants (`agent:read_all`) are deliberately NOT honoured here, including for super-admins: a machine proxy only ever needs its own tenant.

**A 404 means 'no agent you may see is bound to this SVID'** and deliberately covers four cases — unknown SVID, an agent that is not `active` (only `active` resolves; draft, creating, pending, under_review, deprecated, archived and rejected agents all keep their SVID binding and their scores, and none of them resolve), an agent in a team you cannot read, and an SVID ambiguously bound to more than one agent. They are distinguished in Console's logs and never in the response, so this endpoint cannot be used to enumerate SVIDs across tenants.

**Expected consumer behaviour:** 404 → deny the call (fail closed). 401 → re-exchange the API key at `POST /v1/auth/token`, retry once, then deny. 403 → deny. 5xx or timeout → deny, retryable.

**Forward compatibility:** consumers MUST ignore unknown fields and MUST treat an unrecognised enum member as untrusted and fail closed. New fields and new enum members are additive changes and will ship without a version bump.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>`.

Submit the SDK-computed trust score for a LOCAL-mode evaluation.

VIJIL-806 — vijil local-mode v1, Option Z closing-the-loop endpoint.
The Vijil SDK calls this after running a harness on the developer's
laptop:
  1. POST /v1/evaluations → eval_id (Commit 3)
  2. GET /v1/harnesses/{name}/detector-map → rows (Commit 4)
  3. SDK runs rows × agent × /v1/detect → per-row verdicts
  4. SDK aggregates verdicts into a trust score
  5. POST /v1/evaluations/{eval_id}/score ← this endpoint
  6. Workflow transitions to SUCCEEDED, eval shows up in fleet view

Validates the workflow is a LOCAL eval in awaiting_local_score phase
(rejects second-POST attempts as 409 Conflict). Persists results to
EvaluationStorage BEFORE updating the workflow status (the listing
endpoint's dedup-prefers-storage rule depends on this ordering).

Args:
    evaluation_id: Evaluation ID from the prior create call.
    request: Score payload (team_id, behavioral_score, optional
        harness_results + summary).
    claims: JWT claims with user info.
    diamond_domain: Diamond domain orchestrator.

Returns:
    SubmitLocalScoreResponse with evaluation_id and final status.

Raises:
    HTTPException:
      - 403 if user lacks evaluation:create permission for the team
      - 404 if no evaluation with this id exists for the team
      - 400 if the eval is not a LOCAL evaluation
      - 409 if the eval is not in awaiting_local_score phase
        (already scored, cancelled, or otherwise terminal). SDK clients
        SHOULD treat 409 with phase=None + status=SUCCEEDED in a prior
        poll as a successful retry of an already-completed submission
        (idempotency on the SDK side; 409 catches adversarial drift
        where a retry recomputed a different score).

post.summary: Accept a batch of device and application observations from Shadow
post.description:
Write what the batch may write, name what it may not, and acknowledge it.

**202, not 200.** The rows land here; the enrichment that resolves an assignee
runs behind this response (§8.2).

**Partial acceptance.** A record the service refuses appears in ``rejected``
while the rest commit. Failing the whole batch would strand the healthy
devices in it: with no idempotency key and no per-record retry handle, Shadow
could only resubmit the same batch, which would fail the same way.

**No idempotency key** (§A.33). A replay is an ordinary reporting upsert,
monotonic on ``last_seen_at``.

ApiKey.title: ApiKey
ApiKey.description:
An issued API key — what every list/get response returns.

The plaintext `client_secret` is NEVER carried on this model. Use
`ApiKeyWithSecret` for the one moment the secret is visible
(creation).

ApiKeyCreateRequest.title: ApiKeyCreateRequest
ApiKeyCreateRequest.description:
User-supplied input for `POST /v1/api-keys`.

`team_id` and `created_by` come from the JWT context, NOT the
request body — listing them here would let a caller mint keys
against a team they don't belong to. `client_id` + `client_secret`
are minted by CON-477.

ApiKeyWithSecret.title: ApiKeyWithSecret
ApiKeyWithSecret.description:
Response shape for the ONE endpoint that returns the plaintext
secret: `POST /v1/api-keys` (creation).

The plaintext is in the create response and nowhere else: it never
touches the DB (we persist only the argon2 hash — see
`ApiKeysRepository.create()`), it never appears in subsequent GETs,
and it can't be recovered if lost. A "view" endpoint
(`POST /v1/api-keys/{id}/view`) stamps an audit `viewed_at`
timestamp for ops/compliance but returns only the public
`ApiKey` shape — there's no secret to show, by design.

If the user loses the secret, the recovery path is rotation
(`POST /v1/api-keys/{id}/rotate` — generates a new
`(client_id, client_secret)` pair under the same key id), not
re-display. This matches Akrura's argon2-only design choice
(`docs/plans/2026-05-19-vijil-saas-design.md` line 258).

Two structural hardenings:

* `client_secret` is wrapped in `SecretStr` — Pydantic excludes it
  from `repr()` and `model_dump()` unless the caller explicitly
  calls `.get_secret_value()`, which closes the
  "FastAPI debug middleware logged the response body" leak path.
* `model_config` does NOT enable `from_attributes` — this model
  is constructed from `(ApiKey, plaintext)` at the call site, not
  from ORM rows. If a future schema change ever added a
  `client_secret` column to `ApiKeyDB` (which it must never), an
  enabled `from_attributes` would silently pull plaintext from
  the DB row into a response. Disabled here so the attack
  requires both a schema change AND an `__init__` rewrite.

CodeExchangeRequest.title: CodeExchangeRequest
CodeExchangeRequest.description:
Input to `POST /v1/auth/code-exchange`. The CLI presents the
`auth_code` it caught in its localhost callback alongside the
`code_verifier` it generated at the start of the flow; the
endpoint atomically consumes the row and verifies the verifier
against the stored challenge before issuing a JWT.

`code_verifier` is wrapped in `SecretStr` so FastAPI debug
middleware / exception handlers that serialize the request body
don't dump the verifier to logs. The route handler unwraps via
`.get_secret_value()` at the constant-time-compare boundary.

Verifier length is enforced here per RFC 7636 §4.1 (43–128 chars).
Bounding length at the Pydantic boundary returns 422 for
out-of-range input rather than allowing the SHA256 compute on
arbitrary-size payloads downstream (CON-479 Copilot round 2).

AwsAccountStatus.title: AwsAccountStatus
AwsAccountStatus.description:
Whether Console has confirmed the attestor role in the account.

A new connection is ``unverified``: it is the team's CLAIM that it controls the account.
``POST /v1/aws-accounts/{account_id}/verify`` makes Console assume ``vijil-spire-attestor`` in
the account (with the team's external ID) and call ``sts:GetCallerIdentity``; success moves it
to ``verified``, and a definitive refusal moves a verified account back to ``unverified``.

Only a ``verified`` account can carry an agent runtime, and the identity delegate's runtime
read refuses a runtime in an unverified (or unconnected) account with a distinct 409
``runtime_account_unverified``, never as "no runtime".

BadgeCounts.title: BadgeCounts
BadgeCounts.description:
R/S/Sa breakdown of an agent's issues for the home-page badge.

Maps the PRD §4 P1.1 spec ("12 issues: 8R / 3S / 1Sa") to a typed
response shape. The counts reflect whichever tickets the caller's
request returned — by default (no `?status=` filter) the
aggregating endpoint returns tickets across all statuses; when a
`?status=open` filter is supplied, the counts narrow to that
status. The model itself is status-agnostic.

`unattributed` captures tickets whose `dimension` is `None`
(multi-axis clusters, M1/M2-era tickets without dimension); the
frontend renders these as "untagged" in the badge so the total
never undercount silently.

Caller invariant (not enforced at the model level): `total ==
reliability + security + safety + unattributed`. The aggregating
service in `domains/analyzer/service.py` is responsible for
constructing instances that satisfy it; `total` is stored
explicitly (rather than computed) so the response shape doesn't
re-derive on each deserialization.

closed at construction rather than default to a wrong or empty handle.

ScoreIdentity.title: ScoreIdentity
ScoreIdentity.description:
Whether the evaluation that produced a score ran under the SVID being asked about.

``verified`` — the run recorded the same SVID. ``mismatched`` — it recorded a different
one, so the agent was re-bound after the run and the score belongs to a prior identity;
the score is still reported. ``unverified`` — the run recorded no SVID, which is common
and is not evidence of a re-bind.

``verified`` here means STRINGS MATCHED, not identity proven, and the member name is the
only thing about it that suggests otherwise. It is a comparison of
``evaluation_summaries.agent_spiffe_id``, a label the evaluation wrote about itself,
against the SVID in the request. Nothing signed it and nothing constrains it. The member
names deliberately mirror :class:`IdentityVerification`, which sits beside this field and
DOES mean cryptographic proof, so the two must be read together: a run can legitimately
report ``identity_verification='rejected'`` alongside ``score_identity='verified'``, and a
caller that reads only this field would call that run identity-checked.

Two known blind spots, both of which read as ``verified``:

* ``_resolve_agent_spiffe_id`` records the binding as it stands when the run is written,
  and the upsert is ``COALESCE(excluded, existing)``. A re-bind while a run is in flight
  therefore stores the NEW SVID, so the row matches a query for it and the re-bind leaves
  no trace on the score it preceded.
* Resolution and the score read are two statements. A re-bind landing between them cannot
  pair a score with the wrong AGENT -- the second read is keyed on the resolved agent's
  id and team -- but it does mean a ``verified`` answer describes the binding as it was
  microseconds ago. The 300-second cache the response carries widens that same staleness
  by five orders of magnitude, so this is a property of the contract, not of the query.

Whether the SVID this run recorded matches the one being asked about. 'mismatched' means the agent was re-bound after the run, so the score belongs to a prior identity; the score is still reported and the caller decides what that is worth.

'verified' means the recorded string MATCHED -- it is not a proof of identity, and it does not imply this field's neighbour. Read `identity_verification` for whether the run's identity was cryptographically established; a run can report `identity_verification: rejected` alongside `score_identity: verified`. DetectorInputRow.title: DetectorInputRow
DetectorInputRow.description:
One (prompt × detector) test case from a harness's detector_input.jsonl.

VIJIL-806 — vijil local-mode v1. The Vijil SDK consumes these rows to
drive evaluations off-cluster: for each row, send ``forbidden_prompt``
to the agent, then POST the agent's response to ``/v1/detect`` with
``detector_id`` to get a verdict, then aggregate verdicts by
``probe_id`` to compute the trust score.

The shape mirrors the JSONL row from vijil-diamond's harness bundles
with only the SDK-relevant fields projected — id, probe_id,
detector_id, prompt content, plus optional metadata fields that some
detectors need (contexts for multi-turn, role for role-play probes,
kwargs for detector-specific args).

detector_inputs.title: Detector Inputs

DetectorMapResponse.title: DetectorMapResponse

``/v1/evaluations/{id}/score`` (Commit 5).

ProviderErrorCause.title: ProviderErrorCause
ProviderErrorCause.description:
Why a provider call failed, as a closed set.

Deliberately **provider-free**: every value is chosen by us and none is derived
from an upstream response body, because a cause built from a provider error would
echo the probed address back to any holder of ``directory:read``.

The split that matters to a client: the first two mean *call an administrator*,
the next two mean *try again*, and ``PROVIDER_REJECTED`` means the provider refused
or garbled this one request, so the same request will likely fail again while the
provider itself is up.

migration, because the column is ``String``.
